$comment: CANONICAL golden vectors for the CID utility rank. THE single source of truth.
The rank decides which of a record's several CIDs is elected canonical - the cid a
record is advertised and addressed by. It is reimplemented in Go, 2x Rust and 3x TS;
they cannot share code (independent submodules, no cargo path-dep). These vectors are
the only thing holding them in sync: every implementation's test suite loads this file.
This file is VENDORED into each consuming submodule (submodule CI cannot read above its
own tree). scripts/check-cid-vectors.sh diffs every copy against this one.
Ranking is by UTILITY for external retrieval, not cryptographic strength.
Ties break on the lexicographically smaller cid, so the election is deterministic
across peers and does not churn.

ladder.30: sha2-256 / sha3-256 / sha3-384 - real content digests
ladder.25: nzb-posting - content-derived (Message-ID set digest), but not itself fetchable
ladder.5: opaque locators (nzb-release, url) - never outrank a real digest

vectors.name: ipfs-dagpb
vectors.note: dag-pb codec 0x70 - chunked IPFS file, broadest network reach

vectors.name: sha2-256-raw-codec
vectors.note: fullhash/gateway convention: raw codec 0x55, mh names the algo

vectors.name: sha2-256-codec-eq-mh
vectors.note: REAL meta-hash fixture; meta-hash sets codec == mh

vectors.name: nzb-posting
vectors.note: codec 0x1003 + REAL sha2-256 multihash (0x12) over the normalised, sorted Message-ID set - NOT a locator, so it sits ABOVE tier 5, but it addresses no fetchable block (bitswap can never satisfy a want for it - the digest is over an id set, not over any block's bytes), so it stays BELOW a real content digest (30): once meta-share materialises the media and re-seeds it, that genuine sha2-256 cid must win the canonical election, not this one. Rank MUST match on codec BEFORE falling through to the mh switch, or this scores 30 (same trap as nzb-release/url, in reverse: those need a codec check because their mh is identity 0x00; this needs one because its mh is REAL sha2-256 and would otherwise tie with tier 30).

vectors.name: btih-v2-raw-codec
vectors.note: fullhash encoder convention - SAME tier, both conventions must match

vectors.name: midhash256-codec-eq-mh
vectors.note: the record address; internally meaningful, externally invisible

vectors.name: nzb-release-locator
vectors.note: codec 0x1005 + IDENTITY multihash 0x00. The locator code is in the CODEC slot, not the mh slot - rank MUST match on codec. Tier 5 = below midhash: a locator never outranks a real digest, it wins only as a record's sole cid.

vectors.name: url-locator
vectors.note: codec 0x1006 + IDENTITY multihash 0x00. Same tier/reasoning as nzb-release.

vectors.name: bt-pieces-root
vectors.note: torrent-internal merkle root, NOT a file-identity cid

vectors.name: cidv0-rejected
vectors.note: TRAP: Go rejected this (rank 0) while Rust's MsCid::from_str ACCEPTED it and ranked it 40 (dag-pb). Strict parse = CIDv1 base32-lower only. This vector pins the fix.

vectors.name: token-form-rejected
vectors.note: TRAP: the deprecated <algo>:<cid> token form. Rust used to strip the prefix and rank it 10. It must now be rejected.
